query: Help me understand what's worth analyzing and actionable in these expense records.

per_column.name: asset_category
per_column.rationale: Categorizing spend into hardware/software/cloud/travel types gives a strong grouping axis for expense analysis. Values are well-grounded in short_description and ci; the iPod/ISP row mapped to software_service and the RAM row to peripheral are reasonable readings.

per_column.name: asset_brand
per_column.rationale: Brand extraction supports vendor-level spend analysis, a genuinely actionable axis. Values (Dell, Other) are sound extractions from ci/description text, with 'Other' correctly used when brand is not stated.

per_column.name: travel_related
per_column.rationale: A travel flag helps segment expense types and is actionable, though it partly overlaps with asset_category (travel_equipment). Samples correctly mark False for hardware/service rows.

per_column.name: procurement_action_type
per_column.rationale: Classifying the action (acquisition, provisioning, assignment) gives a useful lifecycle axis. Samples map plausibly from description verbs ('Asset assignment' -> allocation_assignment). The dominant 'registration_addition' default is somewhat generic but grounded.

per_column.name: entry_origin
per_column.rationale: Manual vs auto-generated is only weakly derivable from the given source fields; the basis for labeling a row 'manually_entered' vs 'auto_generated' is not evident in the sampled text, making values partly speculative. Analytical value for the spend query is modest.

per_column.name: has_source_id
per_column.rationale: This is a trivial presence flag mechanically restating the existing source_id column, adding little analytical leverage. It is fully grounded but near-redundant.

per_column.name: ci_identifier_quality
per_column.rationale: Data-quality classification of the ci field (model name vs serial vs placeholder) is a reasonable governance axis and grounded in the ci text ('ISP Services' -> service_name, 'OptiPlex 7050' -> descriptive_model_name).

per_column.name: repeat_user_flag
per_column.rationale: Identifying repeat users could support per-user spend analysis, but the flag is near-constant (486 true / 14 false), sharply limiting analytical leverage. Groundedness is moderate since it derives from cross-row user frequency not visible in single samples.

judge.rationale: The added set offers several genuinely actionable axes for expense analysis (asset_category, asset_brand, procurement_action_type, travel), mostly well-grounded in short_description and ci text. Weaker members are has_source_id (redundant restatement of an existing column), repeat_user_flag (near-constant), and entry_origin (labels not clearly supported by the source fields). Overall the columns are useful and largely grounded, with one flag showing speculative values.
